requirement_text.REQ-152: Deny all four ambient Lua time sources (os.time, os.date, os.clock, os.difftime) and implement platform.now() (LUA-14 restated). See docs/requirements.yaml REQ-152 for full text and acceptance_criteria.

acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion in docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-152 entry maps to a concrete design element, no TBD/deferrals
Function signatures fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases) including platform.now/0 and the TimeSource behaviour
Sandbox-denial mechanism is unambiguous and specifically explains why it avoids the :sandboxed trap
Cross-module dependencies listed (sandbox.ex, platform.ex, Lua.new/1 integration point)
No implementation code present (no .ex code blocks with bodies -- signatures/type shapes only)
The design's own flagged OQ-1 (os.setlocale not actually denied by REQ-151 despite its description) is handled as a genuine open item, not silently smoothed over
PASS or FAIL with specifics; route to ELIXIR-DEV (2a) on PASS, back to CODE-DESIGNER on FAIL

checks.check: All 8 REQ-152 acceptance criteria map to a concrete design element, no TBD/deferrals
checks.notes: Section 6 traces all 8 ACs verbatim against §2.2, §2.4, §3.1-3.3, §4, §5. AC8 (mix test/compile) is correctly deferred to ELIXIR-DEV's Step 2a as a not-design-time artifact, not a design gap. Open questions (§11 OQ-2..OQ-4) are all explicitly non-blocking and outside the 8 ACs, not deferrals of required scope.

checks.check: Function signatures fully specified (name, inputs, outputs, error cases), including platform.now/0 and the TimeSource behaviour
checks.notes: §3.1 now/0 :: iso8601_utc(), explicit never-fails reasoning (no I/O, no user input). §3.2 TimeSource @callback now() :: DateTime.t(), SystemClock default impl, application-env resolution key named exactly (:letflow, :lua_platform_time_source). §4.1 install/1 :: Lua.t() -> Lua.t(), mechanism (Lua.set!/3) and composition point (§4.2) both concrete.

checks.check: Sandbox-denial mechanism unambiguous and avoids the :sandboxed trap
checks.notes: §2.4 restates the trap and states the fix precisely: 5 new entries appended to the same @sandbox_deny_set module attribute REQ-151 defined, one Enum.map derivation unchanged, single Lua.new/1 call site preserved (INV-SBX-1 unaffected). Verified directly against lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex: the real deny-set is 28 entries via one Lua.new(sandboxed: ...) call, matching the design's described mechanism exactly.
§8 table covers Sandbox→Platform, Platform→TimeSource, Platform→SystemClock, Platform→Lua (deps/lua), REQ-153 consumer, and REQ-157/159/160 future extension point, each with direction and nature.
Only @type/@spec/@callback signatures and moduledoc content obligations shown. now/0's body is explicitly called out as 'not shown -- implementation' (§3.2) and left to ELIXIR-DEV.

checks.check: OQ-1 (os.setlocale not actually denied by REQ-151) handled as a genuine open item, not silently smoothed over
checks.notes: Verified independently against lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex: the real @sandbox_deny_set (28 entries) has no [:os, :setlocale] entry -- setlocale is only named inside a reason string describing os.execute's vacuity, confirming the design's finding is accurate, not fabricated. §11 OQ-1 states the finding, states the design's own disposition (close it in REQ-152, §2.2 row 5) as a deliberate scope decision already made -- not left ambiguous for ELIXIR-DEV -- while flagging the REQ-151/REQ-152 boundary call for this gate's and SECURITY-REVIEWER's confirmation. This gate confirms the disposition is correct: REQ-152's own AC3 requires os.setlocale tested from inside a script, REQ-152 already extends the same sandbox.ex module and deny-set list REQ-151 defined, and REQ-151 has already merged, so closing the gap in REQ-152 rather than reopening a merged requirement is the right call.

cross_checks_performed: Read lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex directly: confirmed 28-entry @sandbox_deny_set, confirmed 6-of-11 os functions denied (execute/exit/getenv/remove/rename/tmpname), confirmed no [:os,:time/:date/:clock/:difftime/:setlocale] entries -- matches design §2.1's count exactly
Read docs/requirements.yaml REQ-152 entry in full: all 8 acceptance_criteria quoted verbatim in the design's §6 match the source text

Read lib/letflow/design/req151-lua-sandbox.md §0 and moduledoc-equivalent framing: LUA-03/LUA-04 restatement style, :sandboxed trap description, and deny-set construction mechanism are consistent with what REQ-152's design extends
result.verdict_summary: PASS. All 8 REQ-152 acceptance criteria map to concrete, unambiguous design elements with no TBD/deferral language on in-scope items. Function signatures (platform.now/0, TimeSource callback, install/1) are fully specified including error-case reasoning. The sandbox-denial mechanism explicitly and correctly avoids the :sandboxed-replaces-defaults trap by appending to the existing @sandbox_deny_set rather than constructing a second/partial list, verified consistent with the real sandbox.ex. Cross-module dependencies are enumerated. No implementation code (.ex bodies) is present -- signatures and type shapes only. OQ-1's os.setlocale gap-closure finding was independently verified against sandbox.ex as accurate, and is handled as a genuine, resolved design decision flagged for gate confirmation, not silently smoothed over.
